To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the crystal structure of a new organic salt, namely allylamine hydrogen succinate, which is the first example of an organic salt containing a succinate anion.
the title compound, allyl-ammonium hydrogen succinat, crystallizes in the monoclinic space group P21/c with Z = 4, a = 5.8840 (4), b = 9.1695 (5), c = 12.5956 (9) Å, β = 94.808 (3)∘.

the crystal structure of the title compound consists of two allyl-ammonium cations (with syn-periplaner and gauche conformations) and two hydrogen succinates, and that the packing is characterized by two very short, almost linear O—H ⋯ O hydrogen bonds forming helical chains along [011], which are further linked through N—H ⋅ O hydrogen bonds to form layers lying parallel to the (100) plane.

the synthesis and crystal structures of allylammonia salts with succinate anions.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the title compound is an excellent candidate to be used as a model compound for the study of the hydrogen-bonded structures in the solid state, as it is a simple system with a high degree of structural variability.
, while allylamine and its salts are well studied, allylamine hydrogen succinate has not been reported previously, and the crystal structure of the title compound is reported here for the first time.

the crystal structure of the title compound is not a simple one, but is instead a very complex one, with the presence of a large number of weak interactions (including C–H⋯X, O–H⋅⋅⨯O and N–H⋮O) and the formation of a three-dimensional network of intermolecular interactions.
